subject: Tyska
title: Grammar: accusative case
sourceSummary: The accusative form of the definite and indefinite article, plus personal pronouns in the accusative.

questions.prompt: Which article changes in the accusative compared to the nominative?
questions.opener: Only one of the three genders changes.
questions.explanation: Only masculine changes in the accusative: "der" becomes "den". Feminine (die) and neuter (das) look the same in the nominative and accusative.

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Ich sehe ___ Hund." (der Hund = the dog, direct object)
questions.opener: "Hund" is masculine and is the object here — what changes then?
questions.explanation: "Hund" is masculine and is the object of the sentence (what you see), so the article becomes accusative: "den Hund".

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Ich kaufe ___ Buch." (das Buch = the book, direct object)
questions.opener: "Buch" is neuter — does the article change in the accusative?
questions.explanation: Neuter doesn't change in the accusative: "das Buch" is the same in the nominative and accusative.

questions.prompt: Choose the right indefinite article: "Ich habe ___ Bruder." (der Bruder, direct object)
questions.opener: "Ein" changes to "einen" for masculine in the accusative.
questions.explanation: "Ein" becomes "einen" for masculine in the accusative. "Eine" (feminine) doesn't change in the accusative.

questions.prompt: Choose the right pronoun: "Ich sehe ___." (I see him.)
questions.opener: "Er" (he) becomes a different word in the accusative.
questions.explanation: "Er" (he, nominative) becomes "ihn" in the accusative: "Ich sehe ihn" (I see him).

questions.prompt: Write the accusative form of "ich" (I) — the same word as "me".
questions.opener: One of the pronouns that actually changes the least.

questions.prompt: Correct the error: "Ich brauche der Stift." (I need the pen.)
questions.opener: "Der Stift" is masculine and is the object of the sentence.
steps: "Der Stift" (the pen) is the object of "brauchen" (to need), so it should be in the accusative.

questions.prompt: How does the accusative work in German, and which articles/pronouns change?
questions.opener: Only masculine changes — everything else is like the nominative.
questions.answer: The accusative is used for the direct object (the one "receiving" the action). Definite article: der → den (masculine, the ONLY one that changes), die/das/die unchanged. Indefinite article: ein → einen (masculine), eine/ein unchanged. Personal pronouns: ich→mich, du→dich, er→ihn, sie→sie, es→es, wir→uns, ihr→euch, sie→sie. Examples: "Ich sehe den Hund" (I see the dog), "Ich liebe dich" (I love you).
